name: The Materials That Made Civilization
description: From a chipped stone to the silicon crystal: the stone, clay, metals and plastics that shaped how people lived.

checkpoints.name: Stone and fire
checkpoints.note: The first tools are chipped stones. Later people learn to bake clay into pots and bricks, which makes storage, cooking and building possible.

checkpoints.name: Metals and glass
checkpoints.note: Copper and tin make bronze, iron follows, and glass and concrete appear. Whole ages are named after the materials that people mastered.

checkpoints.name: Paper and porcelain
checkpoints.note: Chinese makers perfect paper and porcelain, which travel west along trade routes. Indian steel and Roman-style building keep their reputation for generations.

checkpoints.name: The industrial age
checkpoints.note: Chemistry and furnaces make rubber, cement, steel and aluminium cheap and plentiful, and cities and railways are built from them.

checkpoints.name: The plastic century
checkpoints.note: Chemists invent plastics and fibres that do not exist in nature, from Bakelite to nylon and Kevlar, and stainless steel and flat glass improve everyday life.

checkpoints.name: Silicon and carbon
checkpoints.note: Glass fibre carries the internet, silicon crystals carry the computer, and one-atom-thick carbon opens a new field of materials.
